name: zxcc
desc: CP/M 2/3 emulator for cross-compiling and CP/M tools under UNIX
why: A CP/M emulator under UNIX lets you run eight-bit era toolchains and binaries, a true old-school environment.

brief.what_it_is: ZXCC is a CP/M 2/3 emulator that runs on UNIX, with the stated purpose of letting Hi-Tech C for CP/M be used as a cross-compiler under UNIX. It also lets the CP/M build tools (MAC, RMAC, GENCOM, LINK) run under DOS or UNIX. It is built on two libraries: CPMIO handles terminal emulation (VT52, VT100, or native), and CPMREDIR maps host directories to CP/M drives. The homepage does not describe command-line usage, so the executables listed in the package metadata (zxas, zxc, zxcc, zxlibr, zxlink) are not confirmed from the page.
brief.why_it_exists: The author wants eight-bit-era CP/M development tools to keep working on modern machines, so that CP/M compilers and build tools can be used for cross-compiling without a real CP/M system.
brief.how_it_works: CPMREDIR makes directories on the host system appear as CP/M drives, and ZXCC uses it for all drives. CPMIO provides terminal emulation, with multiple emulation modes modelled on MYZ80 under DOS. The page says the two libraries are LGPLed and can be used separately, and that CPMREDIR is also used in the JOYCE PCW emulator.
brief.install_notes: The stable 0.5.7 release is distributed as zxcc-0.5.7.tar.gz and builds with the GNU Autotools. It bundles development versions of CPMIO and CPMREDIR, so they do not need to be downloaded separately. CPMIO 1.1.1 and CPMREDIR 1.1.1 are also published as separate tarballs. The page gives no download URLs beyond these filenames, and no runtime or configuration steps.
brief.standout: It is a CP/M emulator built for toolchains rather than games or retro nostalgia, and its terminal and filesystem layers are split into reusable LGPL libraries. The author notes that CPMREDIR is also used in his JOYCE PCW emulator.
brief.status: Quiet. The homepage footer is dated 2013-12-28 and is signed by John Elliott. The page shows no later release or commit information, so the current state is unknown beyond that.
brief.caveats: Version 0.5.7 has not been built or tested on DOS, according to the author. The older 0.4.0 release is free for non-commercial use only and needs CPMIO and CPMREDIR compiled separately. The GPL/LGPL split between versions is a licensing consideration. The homepage describes no features beyond terminal emulation and filesystem mapping, and no documentation beyond this single page was fetched. Homebrew reported no caveats.
